notes.title: Devlog: Endless Mode and More Story Chapters!
notes.content:
Greetings Innkeepers!

Over the past month, we've been developing two very crucial and exciting aspects of Dungeon Inn — the Endless Mode and even more story chapters! We know that many of you are waiting with bated breath for these features so we want to ensure that we implement them well.

[h2]Facility Uprades[/h2]
Endless Mode took quite a lot of brainstorming, testing and revision and we believe that what we have will be something that you will greatly enjoy. While we were working on the Endless Mode, we decided to adjust the facility upgrades to give them a bigger and more strategic role in both the Endless Mode and the Story Mode. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/3d4ce807e89809d746a2a4a23575585e75ed37d6.png[/img]

Previously, there was little distinction gameplay-wise between the different facilities and the effects of each upgrade was relatively simple. That is why we have reworked the functions and effects of facilities. Within the Endless Mode specifically, it will serve as a stage-based reward that will also be closely tied to skill enhancements. 

[h2]Story Continuation[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/69860e977eb9870360442fc5c77edb0c0eae935a.png[/img]
We absolutely have to continue the story of Dungeon Inn! Many of you have been wondering what kind of threat and perils Chever, our Chestnut Detective, will bring to the Dungeon Inn! And how will Sara and her friends handle the upcoming challenges? Well... We are just as curious as you are!

The biggest challenge while working on the upcoming story chapters was making sure that the narrative and the level design worked well together! The narrative and the gameplay have to mesh well and make sense together. Simultaneously, we had to ensure that each stage felt well-balanced for players so the game will not feel too difficult or too easy. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/e6a98e9185ac6e0fb8466fa2371e1fc4e823fe8e.png[/img]

Please stay tuned for our Endless Mode and the new chapters! We cannot wait to show you what we have been working on, and hearing from all of you.

As usual, every suggestion and feedback matters to us! If you have any other questions or comments, we would be delighted to hear from you through [url=https://forms.gle/LBSwV1LvRiZx3DNs7]this Google form[/url].

notes.title: Devlog: Working on Endless Mode
notes.content:
Hello Innkeepers! 

Can you believe it? [h3]It's going to be... May![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/68d30d7ed798720997672f7b5d7a6f8ca7a121bd.gif[/img]

Okay, okay, enough jokes! Let's get straight into what we've been up to lately.

[h2]Endless Mode[/h2]
We are excited to announce that we are currently working on an Endless Mode! Many innkeepers have told us they enjoy our main game mechanic a lot and have requested for this feature to be included. 

We are currently developing the prototype for this mode, and it is definitely not without its challenges. It was quite difficult to separate the structure of the Endless Mode so that it does not conflict with the existing system in Story Mode.

On top of that, we had to put in a lot of effort to ensure that the charm and fun of Story Mode was well-translated into the Endless Mode as well, all while also ensuring that Endless Mode still offered distinct features and details. That is why we are making a more dynamic suspicion level to make Endless Mode feel more suspenseful and dynamic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/ed8176bfad8c58ddd6bb9e3d1bd6552d3f146f60.png[/img]

[h3]Features we will include:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Adding a simple event system, such that a simple event will be triggered when a certain number of guests visit
[*] Setting rules so that the black market will occur more frequently. When the number of deaths in battle exceed a certain number, a black market event will occur
[/list]
With all the work and consideration going into this feature, it looks like we'll need a little more time to get the infinite mode ready for you all. Right now, we're still working on a prototype, and after some internal testing and tweaking, we'll be ready to open it up for public testing! 

Thank you to all the lovely innkeepers who suggested including an endless mode to the game. We are working hard to create a feature that our players will love and enjoy, so we hope you'll be excited too!

[h2]Monthly Goal System[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/91a74f1272d9784947efe749e7b9f1e452f226c1.jpg[/img]

Finally, in the previous update, we added a Monthly Goal System to make the monthly/chapter ranking easier to understand for players. This is after innkeepers have expressed that they didn't really understand how they were being ranked by Mr Dragon.

How did you find the Monthly Goal System we added? We hope that it has helped to make the ranking system in our game clearer. Please let us know your thoughts!

As always, we would absolutely love to hear your suggestions and feedback as it is invaluable to helping us improve the game. If you have any other suggestions or bugs, we would be delighted to hear from you through [url=https://forms.gle/LBSwV1LvRiZx3DNs7]this Google form[/url].

notes.title: Devlog: Welcoming Spring and New Master Adventurers!
notes.content:
Hello Innkeepers!

Spring is peeking around and we've got little plant friends for our studio to welcome it. And you'll also be glad to hear that we will also be welcoming some new guests at the Dungeon Inn!

[h2]Adventurers Incoming![/h2]

We have been hard at work creating new Master Adventurers and their visitation events. We'll continue to add more and more Master Adventurers! 

Here's a sneak peek into some of the characters and events we have prepared:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/9e341325b2b3e18a9a47dcb4699b12d30a5076ce.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/f95f51090bff39ff2302890f4240a9edd5c31336.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/09157b9d33cdedeeb13394e2a59fb7722e8a0cc1.png[/img]

Our end goal is to include 30 of them in the game. We put in a lot of thought into crafting each and every one of our adventurers, but especially our Master Adventurers, so that each of them will be a unique and interesting guest to the inn! 

We also have two more super interesting adventurers that will be added to the roster soon!

And what's so interesting about them? Well, they were born from our players' suggestions! Here are the lovely characters that came from your suggestions

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/c7187f2981ebe2a8ed100bbbc3e421c49f5e0a0c.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/b63cbbcce71a6e95e49813580d65ac03825a682c.gif[/img]

We'd love to thank everyone for your enthusiastic participation! We saw a lot of incredible ideas and we really had a hard time picking these two from all the amazing suggestions. We will treat our bug and pumpkin mages with a lot of care and we hope you'll be nice to them when they visit your inn!

[h2]Monthly Tribute[/h2]
Next, we will be working on changing the calculation method of the Monthly Rank by adding monthly target amount and revising the criteria for the monthly rewards (i.e. the special tokens). Currently, the existing rank calculation method was too simplistic and it might get boring if it has to be repeated 12 times through the game. We also wanted to avoid players' low performance in the first one or two stages hindering them for the rest of the game. 

That is why we are restructuring the goals such that they are more motivating than punishing for you! We want Dungeon Inn to be a fun game for you and so we created a more dynamic reward system.

We've also made it such that the conditions for achieving the monthly goal are only affected by the current difficulty level. Previously, the monthly target amount varied depending on the week of the month that you change the difficulty level. That is why we believe that this change will make the game more manageable for those who decide to change the difficulty level later on in the game!

We hope the changes we've made to the monthly goals will be well-received by you, and that it will help make Dungeon Inn's game experience much smoother!

As usual, thank you so much for all your support!

notes.title: A Sneak Peek of Our Future Gamedev Plans!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/ec67db75df401928024879fdda1aebdc1f932294.jpg[/img]

Hello Innkeepers!

It has been a month since the release of Dungeon Inn in early access, and the game’s Steam ratings seems to have stabilized at 92% positive reviews, and for that, we are incredibly touched. From the bottom of our hearts, we thank every single one of you for your support and invaluable feedback.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/9562da326ba49bfe9b5c8c2dc28fe6ae7f6fd65f.png[/img]

Ever since our early access release, we have fixed a number of bugs reported by our players, optimized the UI and localization, and improved the game’s overall experience. Following that, we are happy to announce that we are working on the features and items we mentioned in our roadmap. We are excited to share all this exciting new content with you in the near future!

Based on some of our players’ suggestions and feedback, these are the future plans for Dungeon Inn:

[h2]1. Room customization[/h2]

Many players have asked us to add room customization options. After some discussion, we have decided that this would be a terrific idea! In the future, we plan to allow players to unlock decorations and customize Sara’s room, giving a personal touch to your inn.

[h2]2. Full release's game length [/h2]

As we are experimenting with a unique gameplay, we wanted to collect feedback as early as possible to make sure Dungeon Inn will be fun for all of you! Hence, we chose to release it as an early access game. The current version is about a quarter of the full release’s intended amount of content. In the future full release, we plan to add more story chapters and even an endless mode, making the game’s length approximately 20 hours. (For a more detailed description of our update plans, please see the roadmap on our store page.)

For those who have already purchased the game in early access,  rest assured there will be no additional fees and you will be able to enjoy the full release version with all its updated content for free. Once again, thank you for your patience and support!

[h2]3. Inn facilities and their upgrades will have a greater effect [/h2]

We have received feedback from players that adding and upgrading inn facilities did not have a noticeable effect. After some discussion, we intend to make the effect of upgrades more obvious. For example, we will be adding more abilities that will be unlocked through upgrading the inn, increasing the number of special events that are related to the inn facilities and their rewards, as well as enhancing the strategic experience and so on.

Please note that these changes will be rolled out gradually and incrementally, and we will be closely monitoring player feedback and making adjustments accordingly. This is to ensure that the full version’s upgrading system will be more interesting and satisfying!

[h2]4. Improving the game’s saving function [/h2]

Players have brought up the lack of save files for the final week. To resolve this, we will be implementing the save function for week 16 to ensure that when we update the game with new story chapters, there will be no need to replay previous chapters. Simultaneously, we will also provide an official save file that players can use to start the game directly from the latest point in the game.

Additionally, we will be adding a quick save slot that can be accessed from the main menu. Do you need to quit the game while you were in the middle of a stage? Or maybe you want to freely adjust your business strategies by loading mid-stage save files? With our upcoming quick save slot, you can save in the middle of stages without worries of losing your current progress!


Once again, thank you everyone for your valuable feedback! Of course, on top of the abovementioned points, we will also be continuously optimizing the game’s difficulty level, adjusting weekly goals, improving the game’s UI, as well as gradually adding more and more adventurers, special events, challenges as well as exciting story development! We welcome our fellow innkeepers to keep an eye on this space as we update you on our progress!

Don't forget — every suggestion and feedback matters to us! If you have any other questions or comments, we would be delighted to hear from you through [url=https://forms.gle/LBSwV1LvRiZx3DNs7]this Google form[/url].

notes.title: Demo Update 2024.05.02
notes.content:
Hello, there!
This is Cat Society!


[h2][u]What's in the Update[/u][/h2]

In this update, we've added the following:

[h3][b]Added Difficulty mode[/b][/h3]

You can now enjoy <Dungeon Inn> by selecting a difficulty level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/49be80b34a2d65099f42315faacb9f84e07eeb88.jpg[/img]

You can choose the difficulty level when you start a new game, and you can also change it at any time during the game from the lobby scene.

The difficulty level determines the level of objectives you need to achieve in a stage, and the amount of money you need to send to the Dragon each month. For now, we're keeping the game at two difficulty levels, but we may adjust the number of levels in the future after hearing from players.


[h3][b]Added Monthly Settlements and Commissions[/b][/h3]

Sara's contract with the dragon requires her to send the dragon some (or most!!) of the inn's profits every month. During the last week of each month, she must report to the dragon on how she's been doing!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/7ad4f969c41f7b3663aca1727c70b953bf678d41.gif[/img]

And along with adding a Monthly Settlements scene, we've also improved the Stage Results screen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/c3940a2232af251b53d7f6dec9bb4390bf2febf1.jpg[/img]


[h3][b]Added Selection Constraints by Ability[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/d50d7ce5fb3c5515adeb4828bf0ccb83da32b429.jpg[/img]

When a stage event occurs, certain options will only be available to you if you have a high level of the relevant ability. The higher your each ability level, the easier it will be to make choices that benefit your Inn.


[h2][u]Improved Visual Effects[/u][/h2]

In this build, we focused a lot on making the <Dungeon Inn> more interesting to look at.

First, as mentioned in a previous devlog, we're highlighting adventurers using the Inn on the 'Today's Lodge' menu screen. Previously, we used to show adventurer icons on top of the room/facility tiles, but in this build, we've switched to showing adventurers in motion alongside the faction-specific inn layout.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/86a4a8c68d18db9ab81a5533b20c0ee2e1618c34.gif[/img]

On the stage main screen, we've also enhanced the way we display which rooms and facilities adventurers stay in and use when they visit the inn each turn. Previously, it was simply represented like a log, but we've changed it up by showing the room/facility tiles and putting an adventurer icon on top of them.

notes.title: About the 2024 Development and Release Schedule
notes.content:
Hello, there! This is Cat Society!

We've made it through Taipei Game Show 2024, and then the Steam Next Festival last month. We were blown away by how much more people enjoyed Sara and her friends' story than we expected, from all over the world. It made us very happy and energized! It also taught us a lot about the direction of Dungeon Inn, so we'd like to take this opportunity to thank you all one more time for your interest in Dungeon Inn and for playing it. We'd also like to take this opportunity to apologize for the unfortunate delay in our development schedule.


[h2][u]Delayed EA Release Date (24.Jun. → 2024.Nov.) & Closed Beta Coming soon [/u][/h2]

At the start of the Steam Next festival, we had planned to release Early Access in June 2024. However, after careful consideration of the feedback we received at the festival and the advice we received both inside and outside of the game, we've decided to push the Early Access release date to this fall in order to greet you with a more polished game when it launches. Instead, we're going into closed beta with the build that was originally scheduled for Early Access.

Again, we sincerely apologize for the delay and ask for your patience and understanding.


[h2][u]What's Coming Up?[/u][/h2]

Based on the feedback we received at the Steam Next festival, we're working on the following.

[h3][b]Divide the Difficulty Level[/b][/h3]

[i]"Who should Dungeon Inn be a game for?"[/i]

This is a question we've been asking ourselves since we first announced <Dungeon Inn>.

I think the key to <Dungeon Inn>, and I'm a little embarrassed to say this, is its compelling art and unique gameplay. Art is a first impression. Attractive art greatly lowers the barrier of entry to a gameAnd play is what keeps people in the game, and we're trying to provide original and strategic play in Dungeon Inn.

Here's the problem. Based on the art alone, Dungeon Inn appeals to a light/casual/cozy gamer, but the gameplay is aimed at a midcore gamer. The players that the two elements appeal to are split. One of the things we heard a lot from people who visited our booth at  exhibitions was, "The art looks casual, but the game isn't as easy as I thought it would be." 

At a game show in Korea, one of the things we heard from people who visited our booth was, "The art looks casual, but the game isn't as easy as I thought it would be." Some people said the game was too hard, and some said it was too easy. In that situation, we were developing the game in the direction of making the difficulty a little easier and improving the UI/UX convenience as much as possible to make it easier to understand the gameplay, since we couldn't satisfy all players.

And then after the Steam Next festival. We heard from enough people. And we realized we didn't have to aim for a single point between the two groups. We thought, why not just split the difficulty between easy and hard? People who want to relax and enjoy the story of Sara and her friends can play the easy mode, while those who want a more tense and strategic approach to the game can play the hard mode.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/be6b5d488a7d3a905258f1a396c201098af7667b.png[/img]

There will be some slight differences in level design between difficulty levels, but since it's a story-driven game, the gimmick mix per stage won't change much, nor will the final rewards in the game. We've learned a lot from the Steam Next festival about what people struggle with, and we'll be able to place the right amount of tension and randomization in the game depending on the difficulty level.

[h3][b]Intergrating Fame And Adding Managing Ability EXP[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/2f19df812597b62e5c3781c60a318227bcb0f00e.png[/img]
We're combining the Fame that was divided into 'Entertainment', 'Dining', and 'Dungeoneering' into one Fame, and simplifying the 'Earn basic fame when visiting + additional fame when using facilities' to 'Earn fame when visiting'.

Instead, we've added the notion that using an establishment increases its 'Ability', which is divided into three categories: 'Operations', 'Service', and 'Food', and unlike Fame, is a number that is managed in common across guilds. This factor is used as a condition for purchasing new facilities, as well as to select special options in various Happenings. This skill is primarily increased when guests use the relevant facilities.

[h3][b]Changing Term Around Suspicious : Suspicious Level → Battle Count[/b][/h3]
In "Dungeon Inn", 'Suspicions' and 'Suspicion Levels' are used as threats to detection of double-dealing business. We're replacing the term 'Suspicion Levels' with a more intuitive term, "Battle Count," because the two terms have very similar names, which can be confusing to players and cause translation issues.

[h3][b]More Emphasis on Adventurers Using Inns[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/43c4950075ee695f07207360a6b622a5b133f8a1.png[/img]
In stage, we want to show players how adventurers spend their time when they stay at the Inn. So we're changing the structure and apperance of the Inn's interior, and whereas previously we only showed the adventurer's use of the facility as an icon, we now want to show the adventurer moving through the facility.

[h3][b]Gold Tokens and Sara's Secret Room[/b][/h3]
What happens to Sara's hard-earned money while she's open?

While earning money was presented as a goal in the stages, there wasn't a specific place to spend all the money - it was kind of like a score. Going forward, in each theme, a percentage of the money Sara earns will be converted into Gold Tokens, which player can use like a joker to purchase facilities. And any leftover money will be used to decorate her room!

[h2][u]Upcoming Development Schedule[/u][/h2]
Including the above enhancements, the development schedule for <Dungeon Inn> in 2024 looks like this.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/fccd5f3852669496a1d1bd2ccc572c1bf99dbb78.png[/img]

[h3][b]2024.Apr. : Update Demo[/b][/h3]
The April release will only add the following from the February release.
- Separate difficulty levels, intergrating fame, and adding abilities

[h3][b]2024.Jun. : Do Closed Beta [/b][/h3]
[list]
[*] Add 8 stages (total 12 stages)
[*] Add character skill system
– As the story progresses, each character gains skills.
– You can choose one of the character skills and use it on the stage.
[*] Additional facilities and facility upgrade system
– New facilities will be available to purchase.
– You can upgrade facilities(Normal Tavern -> Sports Pub or Tavern with Bar, etc.).
[*] Add facility usage visualizations
– You can see the adventurers using the facility on the stage.
[/list]
[h3][b]2024.Nov. : Release Early Access[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*] ncorporate feedback from closed beta testing and polish the game.
[*] Add achievements
[*] Add a new stage
[*] New character appears
[/list]
[h3][b]2025 : Release Full Version[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*] We're releasing it with all 48 stages in total.
[*] Reflect secondary elements such as collections, decorations, etc.
[*] Add unlimited mode
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

We're so sorry to announce that we've had to delay our release date once again, following the delay late last year. We appreciate your patience, and we're looking forward to showing you a more polished game.

We hope you'll stick with us and Sara on this journey until the end.

Thank you very much.

Best Regards,
Cat Society

notes.title: Our Next Development Schedule
notes.content:
Hello, everyone!

It's a chilly autumn day here. We thought fall was in full swing when we first registered the demo on Steam last month, but now it's time to take out our winter clothes.

It's been over a month since we released our first demo on Steam. The comments, suggestions, and support we've received so far have been invaluable, and have given us deep insights and inspiration for improving Dungeon Inn in the future.
We'd like to thank everyone again for their interest in and support for our game. We also apologize for the delay in our next development schedule and ask for your understanding.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/f7ce20cfb064197883d81312fd9e98138feea031.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]

[h1]Early Access Release Date Postponed[/h1]
We planned to make the Early Access version with 3 of the 12 themes around the time we participated in BIC 2023 (Korean Indie Game Festival) last August. Our plan was to release early access in mid-January 2024 and full release in late December 2024. However, we realized that we wouldn't be able to participate in Steam Next in February 2024 if we released the game on the original schedule, so we changed the Early Access release date to late February.

To incorporate feedback and make Dungeon Inn more "Dungeon Inn"-like, we decided to postpone the Early Access release date to the second quarter of 2024. We need more time to improve both the quantity and quality of play that should be included in the Early Access version.

Once again, we deeply apologize for the delay.

[i](Dungeon Inn booth at BIC 2023)[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/886da166ec3430cc9127f31e7bd901873344e866.jpg[/img]


[h1]Change in direction: "Focus on the core mechanics"[/h1]

[h2]The need for change[/h2]

[u] - 'Is core play still fun when playing multiple stages in a row?'[/u]

The biggest goal we set while preparing for the BIC 2023 build was to check whether “core play is still fun when playing multiple stages in a row.” While playing through various stages, the player should be able to experience slightly different but continuous play experiences. We also wanted to include elements of the player character's growth, such as the growth of various stats, to reward players for successfully completing increasingly difficult situations.

[u] - 'What kind of gamers should Dungeon Inn be designed for?'[/u]

However, the question that became more important than the results of verification of the relevant elements was “Who loves Dungeon Inn?” At that time, we couldn't come to any other conclusion so just improved UI/UX convenience to help players understand the game. We couldn't collect enough samples from the BIC 2023 exhibition alone, so we decided to wait a little longer after uploading demo builds to markets such as Steam and Stove Indie.

[u] - 'All roads lead to core play, and the paths to get there should be simple.'[/u]

Now that some time has passed, we've decided to focus on core play and keep the other elements simpler. We should remember that every element in our game must enhance the core play.

[h2]How will we develop it?[/h2]
To that end, we plan to develop it with the following contents.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/4b023242ca0baa6bc9d557cffa284adc00f66ea7.png[/img]
[olist]
[*] Suspicion score will fluctuate more dynamically.
[*] Players will be rewarded for exceeding quest goals.
[*] Gold will be limited to goals (a kind of score), and a new currency called "Faction Tokens" will be added.
[*] The department and department placement concept was abolished and replaced with a character skill system (specs not included in the demo build).
[*] The tile placement system for each facility will be abolished and replaced with a tech tree system.
[*] A prologue will be added.
[/olist]
We will provide more details about each item in the next development log.

[h1]Approximate development schedule[/h1]

[u] - 'What is the appropriate amount of content for the early access version?'[/u]

The direction of "Dungeon Inn" has been set, but the amount of content for the Early Access version is still a concern. We have looked at other games, but standards vary depending on the studio, so we need to set our own.

We used to think that a simple introduction to Dungeon Inn and its elements would be enough for Early Access, but after releasing the demo, we realized that it needs to have a larger scale to allow for deeper gameplay. The more we try, the more specific feedback we can get.

Therefore, our current development schedule and development goals are as follows.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44492140/a12723da70bcbe946ff8eb8707950869cec5bb94.png[/img]
[h3]Within 2023: Rebuilding the demo[/h3]
[list]
[*] Rebuilding the current build (theme 1) with the new development direction.
[/list]
[h3]Q2 2024: Early Access release[/h3]
[list]
[*] Include 6 themes.
[*] All major elements that contain core play will be applied to the game.
[/list]
[h3]Q4 2024: Full release[/h3]
[list]
[*] Include 12 themes.
[*] Incorporation of additional features such as collections and achievements.
[*] (L10N) Support for as many languages as possible.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

After releasing the demo build to the market, I was filled with anticipation, but also anxiety. Fortunately we received various comments and suggestions through email, Discord, SNS, and YouTube, and those gave us great strength and great insights. I am truly sorry to announce the postponement of the release date at this time. We will always do our best to show you improved "Dungeon Inn".

Thank you so much for supporting us and Sara on her journey.


Thanks again for reading!
Any and all feedback is appreciated.

- Cat Society
